as_told.title: Puthoff's Physical Review paper on gravity

plain: The physicist Hal Puthoff says his "polarizable vacuum approach," an idea that gravity comes from changes in the properties of empty space, reproduces all the standard tests of Einstein's general relativity. He describes it himself and says he published it in a physics journal. A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, known for unusual patents, praises it on the show without being part of the work: he names the journal as Physical Review and calls the paper on gravity "deserving of a Nobel prize." If the idea works, gravity could be treated as something engineered through space itself.
